literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) derive from the same study (PMC9008429) and describe a single construct type: full-length IFN-γR2 fused to GFP using the 'IFN-γR2-GFP' naming convention, which denotes a C-terminal fusion. IFNGR2 is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein (signal peptide 1–21, extracellular 22–247, TM 248–271, intracellular 272–337). A C-terminal GFP fusion therefore places GFP on the intracellular/cytoplasmic face after residue 337 (L). This is confirmed by the RICS diffusion measurements and PM localization assays in the clips, which are consistent with a cytoplasmic fluorescent label on a surface-resident receptor. No ledger line describes a tag inserted into the extracellular domain (22–247), at the mature N-terminus (after residue 21), or in any extracellular loop. Because the sole evidence is an intracellular C-terminal fusion, zero extracellular surface tag sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion (IFN-γR2-GFP) places the tag after the last residue (L337) on the intracellular face; confirmed by PM localization and RICS diffusion assays in CHO and HAP1 IFN-γR2KO cells.
